notes: Pads: the Designer Drums previews (Ableton's recordings of these Operator pads), names, pans, choke groups, Operator retrigger and osc A's Vel from the set's 'drum rack 1' track.

Balance: a per-onset least-squares fit of the pad previews against Ableton's preview of the whole kit (Phase 4 fidelity review, review/match2.py), at that clip's unknown velocities; 'fit' holds dB and R². 39 is the mean of two fits, 40 has R² 0.79 (low confidence), 42 is its accented on-beat level, 44 is 42 + 4.9 dB (derived: never in the preview; from liverec, below, where the review had 42 + 2.5), 41/43/45/47/48/49/51 are -6 dB (unplayed, unfitted).

Level: calibrated against Live's own recordings of the set (liverec, the Phase 4 comparison of Live's drum takes with SA: SA re-rendered on the patterns of the 28/29 Sep session takes and resampler take 0007, each hit class's band levels set against Live's through the drums strip at -10.6 dB and the reverb at 15.08 %; then all 14 hat, snare and sidestick classes came within 1 dB of Live's). Every Carbon layer plays 10.8 dB over its fit (the kit preview is normalised; high confidence on 36, 37, 40, 42 and 44, assumed for the others), then per pad 36 -2, 37 -0.2, 40 +1, 42 +0.4 dB (medium-high confidence; liverec's -2 dB on 38 had low confidence and is left out). Layer gains: 36: -7.1 + 10.8 - 2 = 1.7; 37: -2.3 + 10.8 - 0.2 = 8.3; 38: -3.3 + 10.8 = 7.5; 39: -3.85 + 10.8 = 6.95; 40: -3.8 + 10.8 + 1 = 8; 41: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 42: -10.1 + 10.8 + 0.4 = 1.1; 43: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 44: -10.1 + 4.9 + 10.8 = 5.6; 45: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 46: -5.7 + 10.8 = 5.1; 47: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 48: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 49: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8; 51: -6 + 10.8 = 4.8.

Velocity: law 'operator', amount = osc A's Vel (Operator's own law is unknown: a linear placeholder), and on 37 1.2, 42 2.4, 44 2.8, 46 2.8 a 'curve': the placeholder's amplitude to that power, anchored at velocity 88, fitted to Live's hats and sidestick at velocities 10 to 127 (liverec; 46, never in the takes, as 44). Kick and snares play only at 88 in the takes: their law is unmeasured.
Beat Repeat: on for every pad whose chain has one on in the set, its band filter where the set's is on. The pads' EQ, Saturator and Compressor are in the recordings; the track's Limiter is not.

Layer: KJ Sawka Drumkit 9 is encrypted; stand-ins by INSTRUMENT from the Core Library's Dry Session Kit (one dry acoustic kit, as KJ9 is): one sample per pad, its loudest take, normalised to 0 dBFS, at KJ9's level; law 'simpler' with KJ9's Vel 0.25. KJ9 has velocity layers only on its floor tom; the Dry Session floor tom has two takes, not four, so one plays on all velocities. 41 layers KJ9's three Snare TT takes, one here. 49 and 51 (rides, unplayed by the patterns) use a short acoustic ride and the Dry Session ride.

Except, from liverec: on 36 Kick Vinyl DLJ 4 at -11.06 dB, not the Dry Session kick at KJ9's level. Live's kick is far brighter than Carbon's (with KJ7 and Kit-Meaty under it alike), 15 dB more at 3-6 kHz even at the right level; this one matched all five of its bands within 1 dB (medium confidence: by band levels, not by ear). On 42 the stand-in, which rings 0.33 s, is cut at 0.075 s: KJ9's Hihat Art 02 lasts 82 ms, and Live's 42 has died away by 80 ms. The layer's level is otherwise not checked: no recording is known to hold KJ9 (they hold Kit-Meaty or other layers, under a Carbon that dominates).
The layer's balance against Carbon is KJ9's level on normalised stand-ins: the Drums tab's layer trim sets it by ear.
Per-pad retrigger is Carbon's; on 49 and 51 KJ9's layer would not retrigger. The layer is not beat-repeated (it is not in the pads' chains).
Not changed by the calibration (liverec): the drums strip (-10.6 dB) and the reverb (15.08 %); no limiter. The levels above hold through them.
